processing_steps.method: vacuum arc melting followed by 4× remelting
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The two steel compositions (M1 and M2) were fabricated using a vacuum arc melting furnace. The melted ingot was remelted 4 times by flipping the ingot before each remelt to ensure complete and uniform melting of the raw materials.
Homogenization of as-cast samples was carried out at 1100 °C for 2 h, followed by water quenching (M2-HQ).
Samples were hot-rolled at 1100 °C to reduce the thickness by 50 %, followed by air cooling (M2-HR). Table 1 lists ~50 % thickness reduction at 1100-900 °C.
Intercritical annealing (IA) was carried out at the selected temperature of 700 °C for 1 h, followed by water quenching. IAT of 700 °C corresponds to ~11 % Mn in austenite for both steels (M2-IA).

structures.overall_structure: Intercritically annealed M2 (Fe-8Mn-3Al-1Si-0.2C) comprises multiple phases similar to the hot-rolled microstructure: α-ferrite and austenite with a negligible amount of martensite; in addition a coarse band-type morphology of δ-ferrite is present due to Si addition.

phases_present.morphology: blocky/plate-like and fine lath/lamellar regions (SEM, Fig. 6)
elongated, banded and blocky regions threading between large ferrite grains (EBSD phase map, Fig. 6b)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: M2-IA: ~92 % of grains in the 0.25-0.5 μm bin, ~7 % in the 0.5-1.0 μm bin, and a small ~3 % population near 1.5 μm (Fig. 8b)

structures.overall_structure: Local microstructural heterogeneity in M2-IA arises from elemental partitioning during IA: Mn and C partition from α/δ-ferrite into austenite while Si partitions from austenite into both δ-ferrite and α-ferrite, raising austenite stability above the equilibrium-composition expectation.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: After tensile testing, M2-IA exhibits strain partitioning into two distinct regions: a low-KAM region indicating lower strain, most likely in δ-ferrite regions, and a high-KAM region indicating transformed martensite (Fig. 11f/h).

interfaces.slip_behavior: Finer austenite grains (γf) with higher Mn and C undergo dislocation glide followed by TRIP at higher strain; coarser grains (γc) transform to martensite earlier (Fig. 12).
interfaces.phase_evolution: On heating M2-HR (α-ferrite + martensitic-austenitic α′+γ + δ-ferrite) to the IAT, unstable martensite first transforms to austenite, then the two types of ferrite may also transform to approach the equilibrium ~30 % austenite; the observed austenite fraction (~19 %) is lower than the equilibrium prediction.
interfaces.interface_notes: Mn concentration profile across the moving α/γ interface during IA at 700 °C: at t=0 flat profiles C_Mn^γ and C_Mn^α/δ; at t=t1 gradients develop between interface and far-field; at t=∞ flat equilibrium steps C_Mn^γ(eq) and C_Mn^α/δ(eq). Mn (and C) partition from ferrite into austenite, Si partitions from austenite to δ-ferrite and α-ferrite (Fig. 9, Fig. 8c).

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog bone-shaped specimen, gauge length 2 mm, thickness 1 mm, width 1 mm (wire-EDM machined)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Uniaxial tensile test on Tinus-Olsen ST25 universal testing machine with 25 kN load cell

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve for M2-IA (red curve) shown in Fig. 10d, plateaus near 700 MPa ending at ~60 % strain.

strain_hardening_rate.note: Value at point B, end of stage-II gradual decline for M2 (IA sample), attributed to deformation-induced martensite transformation (TRIP).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: XRD quantitative phase analysis; EBSD phase maps before and after tensile test

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: PSE (product of strength and elongation) and retained austenite fraction: M2-IA PSE = 41 GPa% and 19 % retained austenite vs M1-IA PSE = 61 GPa% and 45 % retained austenite

characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) in secondary electron (SE) mode
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the multiphase microstructure of M2-IA (α-ferrite, austenite, δ-ferrite bands, negligible martensite)
characterization_methods.key_findings: M2-IA shows a multi-phase α+α′+γ+δ microstructure with retained austenite elongated in bands; negligible martensite; δ-ferrite bands present (Fig. 6a1-a4).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: post-processing with TSL OIM v8.5; National Facility of Texture and OIM at IIT Bombay
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure crystal orientation and obtain phase maps and Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) maps
characterization_methods.key_findings: M2-IA phase map shows α-ferrite, austenite and coarse band-type δ-ferrite (Fig. 6b). After tensile testing, austenite fraction drops to 3.2 % (from 19 %); KAM increases markedly, with strain partitioning into low-KAM (δ-ferrite) and high-KAM (transformed martensite) regions.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: PANalytical Empyrean instrument with Cu-Kα radiation (λ = 1.542 Å)
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification and quantitative austenite fraction determination
characterization_methods.key_findings: M2-IA contains fcc (γ) and bcc (α) reflections; austenite fraction fγ = 19.6 % (Fig. 7).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Samples etched with 2 % Nital (2 ml nitric acid + 98 ml ethanol) for 10-15 s
characterization_methods.key_findings: Optical micrograph of M2-IA shows alternated light/dark bands (Fig. 3).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Tinus-Olsen ST25 universal testing machine (UTM) with 25 kN load cell
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; dog-bone specimen gauge length 2 mm, thickness 1 mm, width 1 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure mechanical properties (strength, elongation) of M2-IA
characterization_methods.key_findings: M2-IA: UTS 698 ± 20 MPa, TE 59.4 ± 0.6 %, PSE 41 GPa%; ductile dimple-rupture fracture.

characterization_methods.purpose: Study fracture behavior of tensile-fractured samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: M2-IA shows dense fine dimples labelled 'Dimple Rupture' (ductile), confirming ductile nature (Fig. 10f).

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fe-8Mn-3Al-1Si-0.2C system; lower critical temperature taken as 600 °C; equilibrium phase fractions and austenite composition as a function of temperature (600-1000 °C).
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted δ-ferrite presence in the ICT range for 3Al-1Si was confirmed by SEM/EBSD observation of δ-ferrite in M2 samples.

analytical_models.equation_role: Select IAT and predict austenite fraction for M2

parameters.name: predicted equilibrium austenite fraction at IAT for M2

analytical_models.model_note: M2 ICT range 600-1000 °C; predicted austenite fraction at 700 °C ~30 % (just above the 30 % gridline, Fig. 2a).

computational_details.simulation_method: Semi-empirical Ms temperature calculation and Koistinen-Marburger model for retained austenite
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Austenite composition (wt.%) at IAT for M2; RT reference.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated retained austenite fraction at RT for M2-IA (~11 %) is lower than the observed (~19 %), indicating additional local-heterogeneity factors.

analytical_models.model_note: Elemental concentrations taken for the austenite phase at hot-rolling/IAT temperatures in wt.%. M2-HR Ms = 296 °C.

analytical_models.equation_role: Calculate fraction of austenite retained at room temperature
analytical_models.model_note: Applied for M2 steel; above the critical IAT the predicted equilibrium austenite fraction is not fully retained at RT.

computational_details.simulation_method: Exponential transformation-kinetics fitting of retained austenite vs true strain
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Austenite volume fraction before tensile test (A) and after fracture; true strain ε.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Fitting parameter B = 3.8 for M2-IA; measured austenite fractions before (19 %) and after (3.2 %) tensile testing used to fit the model.

analytical_models.equation_role: Model retained austenite fraction as a function of true strain (TRIP kinetics)

parameters.name: A (austenite fraction before tensile test, M2-IA)

analytical_models.model_note: f_gamma = A × e^(-Bε); f_gamma = 19.6·e^(-3.8·ε) for M2-IA. Lower B indicates higher mechanical stability and slower TRIP.

unmapped_findings: PSE (product of strength and elongation) for M2-IA is 41 GPa%, compared to 61 GPa% for the Si-free M1-IA; the higher PSE of M1 is attributed to its higher retained austenite fraction and finer grains resulting in slower TRIP (b0006, b0061, b0076, b0083).

The stacking fault energy (SFE) of both steels is below 18 mJ/m^2, a critical value below which the alloys are expected to show a TRIP effect; transformation of austenite to martensite is expected during deformation (b0061).
The retained austenite fraction in M2-IA decreases from 19 % before the tensile test to 3.2 % after fracture, demonstrating the occurrence of the TRIP effect during deformation (b0067, figure_011).

Despite a lower retained austenite fraction, the presence of δ-ferrite in M2 enhances partitioning of Mn and C into austenite at IAT, making austenite more stable; as a result both steels possess a favourable combination of strength and ductility (b0073).

The calculated retained austenite fraction at RT for M2-IA (~11 %, from Ms + Koistinen-Marburger model) is lower than the observed fraction (~19 %); this discrepancy is attributed to local microstructural heterogeneities: preferential segregation of elements (Mn from α-ferrite and δ-ferrite to austenite, Si from austenite to δ-ferrite) and a high fraction of finer grains raising austenite stability above the equilibrium-composition expectation (b0055).

The fraction of finer grains is relatively lower for M2-IA than M1-IA, so the extent of austenite stability would be lower in M2-IA; this explains the relatively smaller difference between observed and calculated austenite fractions for M2-IA compared to M1-IA (b0055).
M2-IA exhibits a ductile dimple-rupture fracture; austenite present absorbs strain energy during deformation by transforming into martensite, forming fine dimples (b0066, figure_010).
